title: Part Four, Chapter 8: Cumarcaah and the Twenty-Four Houses

verses.t: And then they came from there to Cumarcaah, as it was named by the Quichés. And then the lords Cotuha and Cucumatz and all the lords came there; this was already the fifth generation of men since the creation and since they were created. And there they built their houses, and there they also built the house of the god; they set it in the middle of the highest part of the town when they settled there. And then their monarchy grew great again. And they were now many, and then they all decided together to divide, because quarrels had already begun, envying one another over the price of the daughters they gave, and because the drinks were not given to them. And this was the origin of the division, and of arming themselves and throwing the skulls of the dead. And then the nine families or clans were divided; and having quarrelled over their sisters or daughters, they decided to establish the empire in twenty-four great houses. And so it was done, long ago, in this town, when they settled on twenty-four houses there in the town of Cumarcaah, which was blessed by the lord Bishop Don Francisco Marroquín. And there they grew great, and there their thrones and seats were brought together, and they were divided each in his greatness, each of the lords. And each of the nine clans took for itself each of the nine lords; and the lords of Caviquib took nine chinamits for themselves, those of Nihaibab nine, those of Ahan-Quiché four, and those of Zaquiquib two. And they multiplied greatly, and many were those who belonged to each of the lords, and each was the first and leader of those vassals of his, and many were the chinamits of each of the lords. And now we shall tell the name of each one by himself, and of each of the great houses. And these are the names of the lords of Caviquib; and the first of the lords was: Ahpop, Ahpop-camba, 2. Ahtohil, 3. Ahcucumatz, 4. Nimchocoh-canec, 5. Popolvinac, 6. Chituy-lolmet, 7. Quehnayi, 8. Popolvinac-Puhom-tzalatz, 9. Vchuch-camha.
And these were the lords of the people of Caviquib, nine lords, each with his great house in order; and they are mentioned again later.

And these are the lords of the people of Nihaibab: the first Ahanzalel, 2. Ahan-ahtzic-vinac, 3. Calecamba, 4. Vchuch-camha, 5. Nimchocoh-nihaib, 6. Ahan-avilix, 7. Yacolatam, 8. Vtzam-popo-zaclatol, 9. Nima-lolmet and Coltux: nine lords of the people of Nihaibab.
And of the people of Ahan-Quiché, these are the names of the lords: Ahtzic-vinac, 2. Ahan-lolmet, 3. Ahan-nimchocoh, 4. Ahan-hacavitz; these are the four lords of the people of Ahan-Quiché.
And there were two chinamits of Zaquiquib: the one, the lord Tzutuha, 2. Zalel-zaquic; and the two lords had only one great house.
